issues.description: import-notation early-exit ignores params containing both string and url() forms
issues.detail: In lib/rules/import-notation/index.mjs, when primary === 'url', the check `if (/url\(/i.test(params)) return;` bails out as soon as the params contain `url(`. But an @import value could include both a url() and a separate (mis-authored) string token, and even more importantly: when primary is 'url', the rule presumably reports violations on the *string* form. Returning whenever a url() is present means a value like `@import "foo.css" url(bar.css)` (or constructs mixing both) skips reporting entirely. The condition should mirror the violation direction: for 'url', skip when the params contain no string token; for 'string', skip when no url(). The current pair of conditions is asymmetric and the 'url' guard returns on the presence of url(), which is the opposite of what 'url' mode wants to flag.

issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC regex misses fractional and 3-digit numeric weights like 350 or 100.5
issues.detail: In lib/rules/font-weight-notation/index.mjs, HAS_NUMERIC is built only from the keys of NUMERIC_TO_NAMED (100, 200, ..., 900). CSS `font-weight` actually accepts any number in [1,1000], and stylelint's 'named-where-possible' mode should still process declarations with non-standard numerics so they can be flagged or normalized. With `\b(?:100|200|...|900)\b` the early-return will skip a declaration like `font-weight: 350` entirely, changing observable behavior versus the prior implementation which always ran the parser. If the intent is truly to only fix exact 100-step values, this is a behavior change that should be called out in the changeset; otherwise the regex should be a generic numeric matcher (e.g. `/\d/` or `/\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?\b/`).

issues.description: font-weight HAS_NAMED uses case-insensitive `\b` on keywords that may contain hyphens
issues.detail: fontWeightRelativeKeywords includes values like `bolder` and `lighter`, and fontWeightNonNumericKeywords may include hyphenated entries (e.g. depending on the imported list). `\b` does not break around `-`, so a value containing a hyphenated keyword embedded in a larger token could either match unexpectedly or fail to match depending on context. Worth verifying the keyword list contents to confirm `\b...\b` is safe; if any keyword contains `-`, a lookaround like `(?:^|[^\w-])` is safer. Low risk if the list is purely simple words, but it should be checked.

issues.description: keyframe HAS_PERCENTAGE regex is not anchored on the right and is case-sensitive
issues.detail: `(?:^|[,\s])(?:0%|...)` matches the start of a percentage token but does not require a following boundary, so `0%abc` would match. More importantly it's case-sensitive while keyframe selectors `from`/`to` and percentage tokens should be treated case-insensitively to match the rest of the rule's behavior (KEYWORD_TO_PERCENTAGE handling). If PERCENTAGE_SELECTORS only contains numeric forms this is mostly cosmetic, but the right-side boundary issue means the filter is slightly looser than intended. The HAS_KEYWORD regex correctly uses the `i` flag — HAS_PERCENTAGE should be consistent or its asymmetry justified.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation context regex can false-negative on `min-`/`max-` written in feature names with whitespace variants
issues.detail: `/(?:min|max)-/i` requires an immediately-following hyphen. Media features are normally `min-width` / `max-width` etc., so this is usually fine, but values inside feature parens like `(min-width: 600px)` are matched on `atRule.params` which is the entire params string — that's good. However the 'prefix' check `/[<>]/` will also match unrelated `<` or `>` that could appear in comments or future syntax. Risk is low, but the comment-handling case is worth a unit test. Also, when primary is 'context' and exceptExactValue is true, the filter is disabled entirely — verify this is intentional given that exceptExactValue only relaxes a sub-case rather than disabling all filtering.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation filter `/:/` matches pseudo-classes too, weakening the win
issues.detail: The walkRules filter `/:/ ` matches any selector containing a colon — but this rule only fires on pseudo-elements (`::before`, `:before`, etc.). Selectors with only pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`) will still pass the filter and run through the parser. A tighter filter such as `/::|:(?:before|after|first-letter|first-line|placeholder|...)/i` would actually narrow the work, though it sacrifices simplicity. The current change is still a no-op behavior preserver (matches the prior `selector.includes(':')` guard exactly), so this is more of a missed optimization than a correctness issue — but the PR's stated goal is performance, so call it out.

issues.description: Regex constructions from Sets/arrays aren't escaped
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, and HAS_KEYWORD are built by joining keywords directly into a RegExp source. If any future addition to those keyword lists contains a regex metacharacter (`.`, `+`, `(`, etc.), the regex will silently misbehave. A small helper that escapes each entry before joining would be defensive. Not a bug today, but a footgun for future additions.

issues.description: Selector regex filter changes order of operations vs isStandardSyntaxRule
issues.detail: In selector-not-notation and selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation, the prior code called `isStandardSyntaxRule(ruleNode)` before the substring check. The new code applies the regex first (postcss's walkRules filter) and then calls isStandardSyntaxRule. This is generally fine and is the PR's stated intent (consistency with other selector-* rules), but it means non-standard rules whose selector happens to contain `:not(` or `:` will now allocate the matched-rules iteration path before being filtered out. Negligible perf, no correctness impact, just noting the ordering change.

When primary is `'percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block'`, the code sets `selectorRegex = /./` so walkRules still iterates everything. That's functionally a no-op filter (matches anything including empty rule selectors after the first char). It would be slightly cleaner to branch: call `walkRules(cb)` without a filter in that case, avoiding the per-rule regex test. Micro-optimization, but the entire PR is about micro-optimizations, so worth aligning.

issues.description: No tests added or referenced for the early-exit branches
issues.detail: Each new early-exit is a behavior-equivalence claim: 'if the regex doesn't match, no violation would have been reported anyway'. That's exactly the kind of claim that benefits from a regression test per rule confirming that a) declarations that should pass still pass without invoking the parser, and b) declarations that should fail still fail. The diff doesn't include test additions. Existing tests presumably cover behavior, but a perf-equivalence patch deserves an explicit assertion at least in the changeset.

dissents.topic: Whether the import-notation 'url' early-return is a bug

positions.position: Returning when params contain `url(` while primary is 'url' is suspicious — the rule should be flagging string-form imports in this mode, so the guard direction looks inverted or at least incomplete for mixed inputs.

@import params almost always contain exactly one token (either a string or a url()); mixing both is not standard CSS. The guard is fine in practice and matches stylelint's existing token-by-token logic which would not have reported anything in the string branch when a url() is present.

dissents.topic: Whether HAS_NUMERIC in font-weight should accept arbitrary numbers

positions.position: CSS allows any number 1-1000 for font-weight. The filter must accept all numeric values, otherwise the rule silently stops normalizing valid-but-non-standard weights like 350 in 'named-where-possible' mode.
If the existing rule only converts the 9 canonical weights anyway (because NUMERIC_TO_NAMED only has 9 keys), then filtering by the same 9 numerics is exactly equivalent and the optimization is safe.

dissents.topic: Whether the pseudo-element filter `/:/` is too loose

positions.position: The new filter replicates the prior `selector.includes(':')` guard exactly. Equivalence is the right bar for a perf patch; tightening the filter is out of scope.

The PR's whole purpose is to skip expensive parsing. A regex that also filters out pseudo-class-only selectors (`:hover`, `:focus`) would meaningfully reduce parser calls on real-world stylesheets where pseudo-classes dominate.

review.summary: The PR is a straightforward batch of perf optimizations: gate expensive selector/value parsing behind a cheap regex pre-check that should be behavior-preserving. The pattern is sound and consistent with prior similar optimizations in the repo. Main risks are (1) the `import-notation` 'url' guard returns on the *presence* of `url(`, which looks inverted relative to the rule's flagging direction and deserves a test for mixed-token params; (2) `HAS_NUMERIC` in font-weight only matches the nine canonical weights, which is a behavior change for non-canonical numbers like 350 unless the rule genuinely ignores them today; (3) regex sources are built by joining keyword lists without escaping, a future-proofing footgun. The selector-* changes are clean and match the stated goal of moving the substring check into the walk filter. Recommend addressing the import-notation and font-weight concerns (or documenting them in the changeset) before merging.
